topic: AI governance and the AI Act
title: AI Act: what do you owe for each AI system, and by when?
short: List every AI system with your role and its risk class; Annex III high-risk duties start 2 December 2027.
answer: This quarter, list every AI system you use, build or sell with your role and its risk class, and check that none is banned and that chatbots and AI content are disclosed as required since 2 August 2026. Then prepare the duties for any Annex III use, such as hiring or credit scoring, before they apply on 2 December 2027.
audience: Compliance, legal, security and IT leads in EU organizations that use or build AI, including providers of AI systems and models

blocks.title: If you only do five things

items.title: List every AI system and your role in it.
items.text: Record owner, vendor, purpose, data and who it affects, and whether you are provider, deployer, importer or distributor[^aiact]. Running a chatbot you built under your own name makes you its provider[^transp].

items.title: Rule out the banned practices.
items.text: Eight have applied since February 2025, including emotion recognition at work: tracking call center staff's emotions is banned, tracking customers' is not[^aiact][^prohib]. AI that makes intimate deepfakes without consent is banned from 2 December 2026[^omnibus].

items.title: Disclose AI where the law requires it.
items.text: Since 2 August 2026, deployers must disclose deepfakes, and AI text published on public-interest matters that no one edited under editorial responsibility[^aiact]. Customer chatbots must say they are AI; internal assistants for trained staff needn't[^transp].

items.title: Train staff by role and keep a record.
items.text: Since July 2026 you must support AI literacy, not guarantee a level[^omnibus]. Give everyone the basics and people who configure or oversee AI more, and keep attendance lists.

items.title: Find your Annex III uses now.
items.text: Hiring, staff management, credit scoring, life and health insurance pricing, education and biometric identification are among the high-risk uses[^aiact]. Their duties start on 2 December 2027[^omnibus].

items.title: Is it an AI system at all?
items.text: Rule-based software, spreadsheets without AI features and forecasts that just use averages are not[^aidef]. Mark them out of scope.

items.title: Which role do you hold?
items.text: Provider if you develop it, or have it developed, and supply or run it under your name; deployer if you use it[^aiact]. Rebranding or substantially modifying a high-risk system, or turning a general-purpose one to a high-risk use, makes you its provider[^aiact].

items.title: Is the use banned or high-risk?
items.text: Check Article 5 and Annex III. An Annex III system isn't high-risk if it only does a narrow procedural or preparatory task, improves finished human work or flags deviations for human review, unless it profiles people; the provider documents this and registers the system[^aiact].

items.title: Does a disclosure duty apply?
items.text: Chatbots, generated content, deepfakes and emotion recognition each carry one[^aiact]. Record the result, the reasoning and a review date in the inventory.

blocks.title: What each role owes
blocks.intro: Deployer dates are also on the agentic AI sheet.

columns.title: Deployers (most organizations)
items: **High-risk, from 2 December 2027.** Follow the instructions for use, assign trained oversight staff with authority, keep logs at least 6 months, report serious incidents to the provider and inform workers and the people affected[^aiact].

**Impact assessment.** Public bodies, providers of public services and users of credit scoring or life and health insurance pricing assess fundamental rights impacts before first use and notify the authority[^aiact]. It may cross-reference the DPIA[^omnibus].

columns.title: Providers of AI systems
items: **Chatbots and generative AI.** Say it is AI unless that is obvious. Mark generated content machine-readably; systems on the market before 2 August 2026 have until 2 December 2026[^aiact][^omnibus].

**High-risk, from 2 December 2027.** Risk management, data governance, documentation, logging, human oversight, accuracy and cybersecurity, a quality management system, conformity assessment, CE marking and registration[^aiact]; from 2 August 2028 in products under EU safety law[^omnibus].
**Systems already on the market.** Covered only after a significant design change, or by 2 August 2030 if public authorities use them[^omnibus].
**Incidents.** Report serious ones within 15 days, 10 days after a death and 2 days for a widespread infringement or critical infrastructure disruption[^aiact].

columns.title: Providers of general-purpose AI models
items: **Who.** Indicatively, models trained with over 10²³ FLOP that generate language, images or video. Fine-tuning makes you a provider only if it uses over a third of the original training compute[^gpaiguide].

**Duties since 2 August 2025.** Documentation, information for downstream providers, a copyright policy and a public training-content summary; open-source models skip the first two unless systemic. Models placed earlier comply by 2 August 2027[^aiact]. The Commission accepts the Code of Practice as a way to comply[^gpaicop].
**Systemic risk.** Presumed above 10²⁵ FLOP: evaluations with adversarial testing, risk mitigation, incident reporting and cybersecurity[^aiact].

blocks.title: What changed in 2026
items: **The Digital Omnibus on AI took effect on 27 July 2026.** It moved Annex III high-risk duties from 2 August 2026 to 2 December 2027, softened AI literacy, added the intimate-deepfake ban and extended SME relief to small mid-caps[^omnibus][^aiact].
**Transparency guidance arrived.** A code of practice of 10 June covers marking and labeling[^cop50]; guidelines of 20 July give examples[^transp].
**The first harmonized standard was published.** Since October 2026, EN 18286 gives high-risk providers a presumption of conformity for quality management[^hsec].

blocks.title: Who enforces it, and in Germany
items: **Fines scale with the duty.** Up to €35 million or 7% of worldwide turnover for banned practices, €15 million or 3% for most other duties and €7.5 million or 1% for misleading authorities[^aiact].

**The AI Office handles general-purpose AI.** It can fine model providers up to 3% or €15 million since 2 August 2026, and supervises systems they build on their own models[^aiact][^omnibus]. National authorities enforce the rest[^aiact].
**Germany: the Bundesnetzagentur.** Since 29 July 2026 it is the market surveillance authority, contact point and complaints office; BaFin covers AI tied to regulated financial activities[^kimig].
**Germany: the works council.** Inform it in time about planned AI use; it co-determines tools designed to monitor behavior or performance[^betrvg].

blocks.title: Where the AI Act meets the GDPR and the CRA
items: **Run one assessment, not two.** High-risk deployers use the provider's information for their DPIA[^aiact], and the fundamental rights impact assessment may cross-reference it[^omnibus].

**Ask where the model came from.** Models trained on personal data aren't always anonymous. Check that a model wasn't developed unlawfully, starting with its data sources and any regulator findings[^edpb28].
**Bias testing has a legal basis.** Special categories of personal data may be processed where strictly necessary to find and correct bias, under safeguards such as pseudonymization[^omnibus].
**CRA compliance covers AI cybersecurity.** A high-risk system that meets the CRA's essential requirements meets the AI Act's cybersecurity requirement[^omnibus].

blocks.title: What you can skip
items: **ISO/IEC 42001 certification as AI Act proof.** Only EN 18286, which can be layered on ISO/IEC 42001, gives a presumption of conformity for a quality management system[^hsec]. Deployers need neither.
**Inventorying every macro and rule engine.** They aren't AI systems[^aidef].
**AI literacy exams and certificates.** The law asks for measures, not a guaranteed level[^omnibus].
**Labeling internal drafts.** Posts on internal networks and professional correspondence aren't published[^transp].

blocks.title: Mistakes that cost the most
items: **Building CV screening on a general assistant.** It can make you the provider of a high-risk system, with every provider duty[^aiact].
**Emotion analytics on staff.** Inferring employees' or candidates' emotions from calls or meeting video is banned, even during probation[^prohib].
**Relying on the vendor's compliance.** Oversight, logs and worker information are deployer duties[^aiact]. Put instructions for use, log access and incident notice in the contract.

blocks.title: What this looks like at your size

columns.title: Small team, no security staff
items: Keep the inventory in a spreadsheet: tool, owner, purpose, data, role and risk class.
Publish a one-page AI policy (see the AI inputs sheet) and run a short AI basics session each year.
In Germany, use the guidance the Bundesnetzagentur provides for SMEs and start-ups[^kimig].

columns.title: Growing, with IT or security staff
items: Name one owner for AI governance and send new AI uses through a short intake form.
Run the AI Act check, the DPIA and the vendor review as one workflow.
Map Annex III uses and plan oversight training before December 2027.

columns.title: Enterprise or regulated
items: Run AI governance in an existing management system such as ISO/IEC 42001, and add EN 18286 for high-risk systems you provide[^hsec].
Prepare fundamental rights impact assessments for credit scoring, insurance pricing and public services[^aiact].
Track fine-tuning compute against the one-third threshold for general-purpose models[^gpaiguide].
